hints: At the greatest height, the vertical velocity is zero: $v = 0$.
Use the constant-acceleration formula $v = u + at$ with $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
At the highest point, vertical velocity is zero ($v = 0$). With $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$v = u - gt$$
$$0 = v - 10(3)$$
$$v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the constant-acceleration formula for vertical motion under gravity:
$$v = u + at$$

At the instant when the particle reaches its greatest height, its upward velocity becomes zero ($v = 0$). Take upwards as positive, so acceleration is $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and the time taken is $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$0 = v + (-10)(3)$$
$$0 = v - 30$$

Add $30$ to both sides:
$$v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the greatest height $H$ using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0 = 30^2 + 2(-10)H$$
$$0 = 900 - 20H$$
$$20H = 900 \implies H = \frac{900}{20} = 45\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the constant-acceleration formula linking velocities and displacement:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$

Substitute the values:
Initial speed $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed at maximum height $v = 0$, and acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0^2 = 30^2 + 2(-10)s$$
$$0 = 900 - 20s$$
